messages:
jordan: FYI, after today's release /merge to main we're seeing a regression in SSE tail latency on canary 2.
maya: Yep noticed it in the dashboard — p95 up from 80ms -> 240ms for small toolcall streams.
rafael: Bisected to the proto handshake change (commit 0f4a9c), specifically the chunk coalescer tweak that landed with api-proto-v2.
lin: That's the change that delays the first flush to collect tool metadata, right?
jordan: Exactly. The coalescer now waits up to 10ms to aggregate headers+body to reduce small-packet overhead. Unintended effect: head-of-line blocking for SSE frame boundary when toolcall handshake is present.
maya: Repro steps: run curl against /v1/stream with tool=echo and observe initial token delay. Short runs have single-frame responses, so they get delayed.
emily: CPU profiling shows a spike in serializer time while waiting on coalescer timer; KV cache hits drop during the wait which prolongs overall tail.
rafael: Perf top snippet: 
```
Time  Samples  Function
0.42s  512     proto::coalesce::wait_timer
0.28s  320     serializer::emit_sse_frame
0.15s  170     kv_cache::lookup
```
lin: Could be exacerbated by batching heuristics: coalescer inspects batch size and sequence distribution before choosing kernel; if it delays, kernel selection kicks in late and we fall back to generic kernels.
jordan: Reverted the commit in canary-2 and latency recovered immediately.
ops-bot: deploy reverted (deploy-1976543209) by @jordan — canary-2 back to previous image.
maya: CI caught a perf regression on the release branch though, so we need a proper fix before re-landing.
emily: Proposed fix: distinguish toolcall handshake frames vs regular small payloads. For handshake, flush headers immediately and serialize body separately; keep coalescing for non-tool traffic.
rafael: Also tweak KV cache warmup — treat handshake as a cache priming event so subsequent token emission uses cached key-values.
lin: Quick patch uploaded: `coalesce: bypass timer for tool-handshake` in PR #4821. Requesting review.
jordan: If we can't land fast, we should add a temporary rollout rule to route tool-enabled requests to legacy handler until PR is verified.
emily: I'll add a perf regression test in CI that exercises single-token streams with toolcall metadata.
maya: Good. Also add a microbenchmark in eng-runtime to measure coalescer latencies with and without handshake.
rafael: +1. Will coordinate the bisect notes and include the perf top snapshot in the PR.
jordan: Thanks. Heads-up: customers on Dedicated might have seen p99 spikes; ops page updated.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1234 — toolcall handshake canary latency regression.
lin: tagging @security: none of the changes affect auth but worth checking logs for any retry storms.
jordan: Great. Will link PR once CI passes. Short-term: revert stays in place on canary and staging until patch lands. :thumbsup:
